specification.problem: Study how imperfect gate operations (systematic, random, and combined errors) affect Shor's prime factorization algorithm, and determine an error threshold for factoring a given number N.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction of the error-model framing and qualitative findings only; the explicit gate error model, circuit, and threshold formula are not given in the abstract.

symbols.meaning: Gate error strength (assumed parameter for threshold)

equations.label: Error threshold condition
equations.description: Algorithm succeeds when gate error is below a threshold that depends on N.
equations.abstract_quote: Error threshold is given to the algorithm for a given number N to be factorized.
equations.justification: The abstract states a threshold depending on N; the functional form is not given.
assumptions: Threshold treated as a single scalar epsilon_th(N); form unknown.

registers.name: control
registers.role: Holds the phase estimation / QFT input for period finding

registers.name: work
registers.role: Holds modular exponentiation values a^x mod N

specification.initial_state: Control register in |0>^t and work register in |1>, assuming standard Shor structure.

steps.description: Apply Hadamard gates to the control register to create a uniform superposition; each gate carries an error of strength epsilon (systematic or random).
Apply controlled modular exponentiation x -> a^x mod N into the work register using imperfect gates.
Apply an inverse QFT, built from imperfect Hadamard and controlled-phase gates, to the control register.

specification.measurement: Assumed standard Shor readout: measure the control register in the computational basis to obtain an integer y approximating a multiple of 2^t/r; the success probability of obtaining useful y is degraded by gate errors. The abstract does not specify the measurement scheme.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Assumed standard Shor postprocessing: compute y/2^t, use continued fractions to extract the period r, check a^r = 1 mod N, and if r is even compute gcd(a^(r/2) +/- 1, N) to get factors; repeat on failure. Success rate versus epsilon is compared with the threshold epsilon_th(N).
assumptions: Error strength is modeled by a scalar epsilon.
Circuit follows the standard Shor layout; the paper's exact circuit and register sizes are not given in the abstract.
Measurement and postprocessing follow textbook Shor; the paper's specific scheme is not given in the abstract.
